title: Persist the probe-time provider runtime observation durably
description:
Filed by architect-bdaffeaf 2026-08-20 from worker-9cf37223's fc9660b0 gate finding (b) (comment-0975c621, HEAD 06c4e9e): `buildProviderRuntimeObservation` has exactly TWO daemon call sites and both are TEST FIXTURES (goal-closure-test-fixtures.ts:226, foundation-registry-fixtures.ts:197) — zero production writers. The durable provider.probe record persists only {profile, profileDigest, providerMinimumProfileRef, truthClass} (provider-profile-registration.ts:47-58); platformIdentity/reportedVersion/runtime closure appear in NO daemon production file. Consequence: the launch-template producer's `runtimeObservation` input and the service template's `runtime{installedRoot, pinRoot, quotedObservation}` field have no durable server source at the dispatch seam.

DELIVERABLE: on the real provider.probe path (the authenticated ADMIN observation seam — the ONLY caller-proposed seam per the a3e/4d rails), admit and durably persist the runtime observation alongside the existing profile record — the buildProviderRuntimeObservation product (resolved runtime closure digests, reportedVersion, adapterCapabilitySchemaDigest, pinning method, platformIdentity, observedAt) — canonical bytes + digest, same aggregate family discipline as the profile; plus a strict current reader returning it bound to project + probe identity with distinct ABSENT/UNREADABLE/STALE codes. Truth discipline: the observation carries the probe's truthClass; a weak-truth observation reads back but never gains launch authority (the resolver's STRONG_TRUTH gate stays the authority filter).

CONSUMERS: task-fc9660b0 (BLOCKED naming this gap — its dispatch composition reads this record for the producer's runtimeObservation input and the template's runtime field) and the capability-schema evidence chain. MEASURE FIRST at HEAD: the probe handler's current admission shape (bootstrap-services.ts:143 era), the registration module's aggregate/event family, buildProviderRuntimeObservation's exact product shape in @moe/runner. NOT in scope: launch-template composition, mission authority, resolver changes, new wire kinds.
definitionOfDone: provider.probe durably persists the admitted runtime observation (canonical bytes + server-computed digest) alongside the profile, through the existing registration seam — grep for a production buildProviderRuntimeObservation caller (or the admitted-observation persist path) returns a producer where it returned zero

A strict reader returns the current observation bound to project+probe identity, decode + re-encode + byte-compare, with distinct exact codes for ABSENT / UNREADABLE / identity-mismatch at one module-private layer; upstream codes preserved

Caller-supplied digest/closure/version fields never gain authority: identical re-probe is byte-stable; same identity with different observation content refuses with the registration family's immutability discipline (mirror the profile's history-scoped conflict rule)

Real SqliteEventStore tests drive the production probe path (register→probe with nested profile+observation), assert exact code/layer, one accepted control, positive hostile counts; a mutation skipping the digest recompute or the immutability check reds a named test
Daemon typecheck + test exit 0 with nonzero counts; production files <=250 lines with LF bridges; completion names task-fc9660b0 as consumer
taskRails: The probe seam is the only admission door (a3e/4d standing rail); no dispatch-request or optional-override path may supply the observation

Mirror the provider-profile registration discipline: canonical bytes, server-computed digest, whole-history immutability (the 9a6e32c5 QA lesson — adjacent-probe-only comparison is the known defect), module-private layer constants
Runtime observation is EVIDENCE, never model identity (standing rail); the resolver's truth gate remains the sole authority filter

The registration module: provider-profile-registration.ts — PROFILE_REGISTRATION layer (:25), PROVIDER_PROBED_EVENT (:35), providerProbePayload (:47), conflictsWithProfileHistory (:114, the WHOLE-HISTORY immutability rule from the 9a6e32c5 QA round — the discipline this row mirrors). (2) The observation product: buildProviderRuntimeObservation per provider — claude-observation.ts:232, codex-observation.ts:161 in @moe/runner — read the exact product shape (resolvedRuntimeClosure digests, reportedVersion, adapterCapabilitySchemaDigest, pinningMethod, platformIdentity, observedAt, observationDigest?) and verify ROOT publication + the daemon→runner edge (three legs; the daemon already depends on @moe/runner — confirm the two builder symbols are bare-importable or measure what IS: the daemon may only need to ADMIT the caller-shaped product, not call the builder — decide from the shapes and record). (3) DESIGN DECISION to record before tests: the observation persists as a SECOND section of the SAME ProviderProbed event (extending providerProbePayload — one event, one immutability history) vs a sibling event on the same aggregate — prefer the same-event extension IF the existing decode path tolerates the added field version-gated; measure the codec's exactKeys posture on the probe payload first; whichever is chosen, identical re-probe byte-stability and whole-history conflict MUST cover the observation content too. (4) Existing suites pinning the probe payload shape (provider-profile-codec.test.ts :536-era, restore-test-harness PROVIDER_OBSERVATION, affordance-read) — enumerate every fixture this extension touches. Baseline: daemon typecheck + test, separate exits, counts verbatim.
implementationPlan.note:
REJECT PASS — re-measured only what the rejection touches; steps 1-3 of the original pass are on record at c2a1347 + 21f2b85 and are not re-litigated here.

QA'S FINDING REPRODUCES EXACTLY AS WRITTEN, and the arithmetic explains why it sat right on the edge. Canonical JSON per closure entry is `{"kind":"EXECUTABLE","path":"<400>","sha256":"<64>"}` ≈ 507 bytes + 1 separator. 64 entries ≈ 32,512 plus the surrounding record ≈ 32,8xx — a few hundred bytes OVER MAX_OBSERVATION_BYTES = 32,768; 63 entries lands under it. So the runner's own maximum product (MAX_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_ENTRIES 64, MAX_RUNTIME_TEXT_CHARS 400 at claude-observation.ts:22-23) overflows the daemon's durable ceiling by a hair.

THE TWO BOUNDS AND WHERE THEY DISAGREED. `admitProviderRuntimeObservation` (:136) measured nothing; `textOf` (:167) measured `input.byteLength > MAX_OBSERVATION_BYTES` on the READ path only. Everything in between — probe admission, registration, commit — never asked. Hence: accepted, committed, then UNREADABLE/READER with upstream INPUT_INVALID/CODEC on the very next read.

WHY THE ORIGINAL GATE MISSED IT: every existing fixture builds a ONE-ENTRY closure (`runtimeSection`, fixtures :56-69). The suite had no shape anywhere near the ceiling, so 178 files / 3936 tests passing said nothing about the boundary. That is the real lesson here, not the constant.

WHICH FIX. QA offered two. I took the FIRST — enforce the canonical-byte bound at admission with an exact code/layer — and rejected "raise decoding to cover every admitted runner product", with the reason measured rather than asserted: the daemon's text limits are counted in CHARACTERS (512) and its closure limit is 128 entries, both WIDER than the runner's. A ceiling that covers every structurally admissible record has to survive multi-byte UTF-8 (up to 3 bytes/char) and JSON escaping of control characters (6 bytes/char), which puts the worst case near 150KB. Raising 32,768 to that is not a bound any more. Enforcing at admission keeps the durable ceiling real AND keeps the refusal reachable, because the daemon's structural limits still exceed it.

THE TRADEOFF, STATED PLAINLY: a runner-MAXIMUM observation (64 entries × 400 chars) is now REFUSED at the probe seam with PROVIDER_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_TOO_LARGE instead of being committed as unreadable evidence. That is strictly better than today's behaviour and it is fail-closed, but it IS a refusal of a genuine product. If the product wants those storable, raising MAX_OBSERVATION_BYTES is a one-constant follow-up and the boundary test moves with it automatically, because the test SEARCHES for the boundary with the production encoder rather than hard-coding a number.

No existing test pins the read-path over-bound arm (grepped for TOO_LARGE / 32_768 / byteLength across the provider-profile suites — only the reader's own bytesEqual loop matched), so unifying the two bounds into one breaks nothing.

BASELINE at claim: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 (`$ tsc` echo); daemon suite 178 files / 3936 tests, exit 0.

Run: RED.
implementationPlan.note:
FOUR NEW CASES on the production seam, exactly the coverage QA named as missing, in the file QA named. Suite went 26 -> 30 tests.

HONEST ORDERING NOTE, because it matters for how you grade the evidence: on this reject pass I wrote the production fix BEFORE the tests, so I cannot show you a literal pre-fix red run. The equivalent — and stronger — evidence is drill E1 in step 4: it deletes the new admission check, resurrecting the exact shipped defect, and BOTH new refusal arms go red by name. That is what proves these assertions are not vacuous, and I am not going to dress it up as TDD that did not happen.

THE BOUNDARY IS SEARCHED, NOT HARD-CODED. `boundary()` walks the closure-entry count upward at the runner's own 400-character path width, encoding each candidate with the PRODUCTION encoder (`encodeProviderRuntimeObservationBytes`), and returns the pair {largest that fits, exactly one entry more}. Two consequences: (i) the "largest valid shape" and "one over" QA asked for are correct BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by my arithmetic; (ii) if the record shape or the constant ever changes, both cases move together instead of one silently degenerating into a duplicate of the other. The loop is capped below the runner's own 64-entry ceiling and THROWS if no boundary exists there, so it cannot pass vacuously by never finding one.

THE CASE-WAS-GENERATED ASSERTION (epic rail 6, "a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes"): "generates a real boundary pair that straddles the bound" asserts bytesOf(fits) <= MAX_OBSERVATION_BYTES, bytesOf(over) > MAX_OBSERVATION_BYTES, and over > fits. Without it, a boundary() that returned two identical sections would make the other three arms meaningless.

THE FOUR CASES:
1. "generates a real boundary pair that straddles the bound" — the generation proof above.
2. "accepts the largest runner product that fits and reads it back byte-identical" — register -> provider.probe -> readCurrentRuntimeObservation, asserting the read observation equals the section that was sent and that exactly one event was committed. This is DoD 1 + DoD 2 at the size ceiling: accepted evidence must be readable evidence.
3. "refuses one entry more at the codec, before anything is committed" — exact code PROVIDER_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_TOO_LARGE at layer PROVIDER_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_CODEC, PLUS `probedEvents(store).length === 0`. The count assertion is the part that matters: refusing after committing would satisfy a code-only assertion and still be the same defect.
4. "answers a planted oversized row with the same code, upstream of the reader" — a row planted through the store's own API carries an oversized section; the reader answers UNREADABLE at PROVIDER_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_READER with upstream {TOO_LARGE, CODEC}. This is what proves the unification actually happened: before the fix that upstream read INPUT_INVALID/CODEC, and drill E3 (re-adding a second bound on the read path) flips it back and reds this one arm alone.

Fixture added: `sizedRuntimeSection(entries, pathChars)` in provider-runtime-observation-test-fixtures.ts, built through @moe/runner's `buildProviderRuntimeObservation` with the same injected fixed clock as the existing fixtures — the real adapter product, not a hand-shaped lookalike. Paths carry a zero-padded index prefix so they stay strictly ascending after the runner sorts, which is what `admittedClosure` requires.

Two constants are literals in the test with a comment saying why: PATH_CHARS 400 and RUNNER_MAX_ENTRIES 64 are the runner's own ceilings and are NOT published from its root (the fields module already documents that deliberate non-copy). If either drifts, `buildProviderRuntimeObservation` refuses the fixture and it throws — a loud failure, not a silent wrong-shape pass.

THE FIX IS THREE EDITS AND ONE OF THEM IS A DELETION.

(1) provider-runtime-observation.ts — new stable code `PROVIDER_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_TOO_LARGE` on the closed codec roster, and the bound enforced in `admitProviderRuntimeObservation` AFTER the digest recompute and BEFORE the ok return:
  const bytes = encodeProviderRuntimeObservationBytes(resealed).byteLength;
  if (bytes > MAX_OBSERVATION_BYTES) return refusal("PROVIDER_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_TOO_LARGE", ...);
Placement is deliberate on both sides. It measures the RESEALED record, not the caller's, so a caller cannot shrink under the bound by lying about the digest; and it sits below the digest check so a forged digest still answers DIGEST_MISMATCH rather than being masked by a size complaint. The message carries the actual byte count and the bound, which is what an observer needs to act.

(2) The same file — the read path's DUPLICATE bound is GONE. `textOf` no longer re-states `input.byteLength > MAX_OBSERVATION_BYTES`; it keeps only the empty check and the fatal UTF-8 decode. That deletion is the actual repair of QA's third issue: two copies of one rule are what drifted. There is now exactly ONE size decision in the module and both paths route through it, so "admitted" and "readable" cannot disagree by construction. The parse stays bounded independently by `decodeBoundedJsonBytes`, so removing this line does not remove the DoS ceiling — it removes a second, narrower, write-blind copy of a different one.

(3) provider-runtime-observation-fields.ts:43 — the constant now carries the doc QA asked for: why the structural limits above cannot imply it (characters vs bytes; 128 × 512 composes well past 32,768), that it is enforced at admission once and never on the read path, and that an observation too large to store is refused at the seam rather than committed as undecodable evidence.

VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, stated so nobody discovers it later: a probe carrying an observation whose canonical bytes exceed 32,768 is now REFUSED with TOO_LARGE/CODEC and commits nothing. Before this change it was ACCEPTED, committed, and unreadable on the next read. A runner-maximum product (64 × 400) falls on the refusing side by a few hundred bytes. That is a deliberate trade recorded in step 1: the durable ceiling stays real, the refusal stays reachable (the daemon's own structural limits, 128 entries × 512 chars, still exceed it), and raising the ceiling later is a one-constant change that the searched boundary test follows automatically.

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: no new wire kind, no dispatch or override path, no registration or bootstrap-services edit, no reader edit. The probe seam is still the only admission door (task rail 1) and the reader still owns only READER-layer codes — the new code belongs to the CODEC and reaches the reader as `upstream`, which is exactly how the existing UNREADABLE arms already report the codec's verdict.

Line counts after: provider-runtime-observation.ts 208, provider-runtime-observation-fields.ts 124, reader 196 (untouched), registration 158 (untouched), bootstrap-services 215 (untouched). All under the 250 target. No bridge changes — no new module.

This is the drill that proves the UNIFICATION is real rather than cosmetic: put a second copy of the bound back on the read path and the upstream flips from TOO_LARGE/CODEC to INPUT_INVALID/CODEC — which is the observable signature of the two bounds disagreeing again.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE REJECTION, in the order QA raised it:
- Issue 1 (security, observation.ts:136): admission now measures the resealed record's canonical bytes and refuses `PROVIDER_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_TOO_LARGE` at `PROVIDER_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_CODEC` before anything is committed. Placed BELOW the digest check so a forged digest still answers DIGEST_MISMATCH, and it measures the RESEALED record so a caller cannot shrink under the bound by lying.
- Issue 2 (missing tests, observation.test.ts): four production register -> provider.probe -> reader cases using `buildProviderRuntimeObservation`, with the boundary SEARCHED via the production encoder rather than hard-coded. The generation itself is asserted (fits <= bound < over), the at-limit case reads back, the one-over case pins code AND layer AND `probedEvents.length === 0`, and a planted oversized row pins the reader's upstream.
- Issue 3 (fields.ts:43, bounds disagree): the read path's DUPLICATE bound is DELETED. There is now one size decision serving both directions, which is the actual repair — two copies of a rule are what drifted. The constant carries the doc explaining why the structural limits cannot imply it and why it is enforced at admission only.

I CHOSE QA'S FIRST OPTION AND REJECTED THE SECOND, with the reason measured: "raise decoding to cover every admitted runner product" needs a ceiling that survives multi-byte UTF-8 and JSON escaping of control characters against the DAEMON's own wider structural limits (128 entries × 512 chars), which lands near 150KB. That is not a bound. Enforcing at admission keeps 32,768 meaningful and keeps the refusal reachable.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, flagged rather than buried: a probe whose observation exceeds 32,768 canonical bytes is now REFUSED and commits nothing, where before it was accepted and unreadable. A runner-MAXIMUM product (64 × 400) is on the refusing side by a few hundred bytes. Fail-closed and visible beats stored-and-undecodable, but it is a real refusal of a real product — if the product wants those storable, raising the constant is a one-line follow-up and the searched boundary test moves with it automatically.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) A separate provider.observe wire kind — rejected: the a3e/4d rail makes provider.probe the only admission seam, and the union discipline discourages new kinds when an existing seam owns the subject. (b) Deriving the observation daemon-side by running the builder at dispatch time — rejected: the builder observes the HOST at probe/launch time; dispatch-time synthesis would be fresh observation wearing durable clothes.
